content: Melvin-Koushki reports that Nafsat I enumerates many examples of the orthodoxy of prominent Sufi masters (fn.103 names ʿAbd Allāh Anṣārī, al-Ḥakīm al-Tirmidhī and Saʿd al-Dīn Ḥamuvayī), dwelling frequently on Khwāja Muḥammad Pārsā (d. 822/1419), the Khwājagānī master and favourite of Shāhrukh.
refers_to_primary: Ibn Turka, Nafsat al-Maṣdūr I, p.173 (per MK fn.103)
